claim: Defines 2026 agent metrics — Tool Correctness, Argument Correctness, Step Efficiency, Task Completion, Plan Adherence — and the outcome/path/component diagnostic stack plus trace-based evaluation.
quote: Trajectory/Path Evaluation inspects the plan, reasoning steps, tool calls, retries, and handoffs that produced the final result rather than just the outcome. Tool Correctness is a deterministic metric verifying whether an agent's tool-calling behavior aligns with expectations.

claim: Gives 2026 production RAG thresholds (recall ≥0.90@k10, precision ≥0.45@k10, faithfulness ≥0.90, answer relevancy ≥0.80), how faithfulness decomposes answers into atomic claims, and the diagnostic decision logic mapping each regression to retriever vs generator.
quote: Recall regression -> retrieval problem; Faithfulness regression without citation accuracy drop -> generation/prompt issue. Faithfulness production target is >=0.90 (unsafe below 70%). Measurement decomposes answers into atomic claims.

claim: Ragas provides the reference metric library — faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, context recall — plus test-set generation, with native LangChain/LlamaIndex integration.
quote: List of available metrics: faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision, context recall, context relevance.

claim: Agentic systems have trajectories, internal state, and tool calls unfolding over time, and 2026 practice distinguishes agent failures from infrastructure failures (a tool API timeout is not the agent's fault; wrong-parameter calls are).
quote: A tool not being able to call an API because of a connection time-out should not be counted against the agent, but the agent not calling the tools with their parameters should be seen as agentic failure.

claim: TRAJECT-Bench shows single-turn evaluations fail to capture agent failures emerging across multi-step trajectories, with failure modes in trajectory length, tool-selection timing, and argument construction.
quote: Single-turn evaluations fail to capture agent failures that emerge across multi-step trajectories. The benchmark identifies trajectory length issues, tool selection errors, and argument construction failures.

claim: Catalogs single-turn-invisible failure modes (ghost actions, confident fabrication, interrogation loops, budget burning), component-vs-end-to-end placement, operating envelopes, judge calibration on human labels, and the stacked-gate CI/regression workflow with production-issue-to-golden loop.
quote: Ghost actions: Agent claims it executed a tool without actually calling it. Apply component checks at tool-call spans, end-to-end checks at the root trace. Fail the run when quality is fine but economics or latency are not. Calibrate LLM-as-a-judge on human labels.

claim: tau-bench introduced pass^k (all k attempts succeed) which decays as p^k — a 90% agent is 57% consistent at k=8, and strong agents score pass^8 < 25% on retail; tau2-bench (2026) adds voice/knowledge-retrieval and dual-control.
quote: pass^k = p^k decays exponentially. A model with 90% success rate drops to just 57% consistency at k=8. Even state-of-the-art function calling agents are terribly inconsistent (pass^8 < 25% in retail).

claim: LLM judges agree with humans ~85% of the time yet exceed 50% error on bias stress-tests; five named biases — position (10-15pt), verbosity, self-preference (10-25%), format, calibration drift.
quote: Frontier models exceeded 50% error rates on bias tests. Position bias causes slot A to win 10 to 15 points more often; self-preference causes judges to score their own family's outputs 10 to 25 percent higher.

claim: A synthetic RAG dataset is (question, retrieved-context, ground-truth-answer) triples; the winning 2026 pattern is synthetic + sampled production + human calibration against one metric set.
quote: A synthetic dataset for RAG is a labeled set of question, retrieved-context, and ground-truth-answer triples that is machine-generated. The winning 2026 pattern is synthetic + sampled production + human calibration.

claim: A golden dataset is a curated, versioned source-of-truth collection of prompts/inputs/contexts/expected-outcomes; domain experts author must-pass scenarios with explicit acceptance criteria as anchor tests.
quote: A golden dataset is a curated, versioned collection of prompts, inputs, contexts, and expected outcomes that becomes the source of truth for measuring quality across your AI lifecycle.

quote: Ragas: Supercharge Your LLM Application Evaluations.
